Round 2 of the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json (NOT page.research-acetyl-*; the template still carries the Argireline trade name), section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Round 1 is kept at 2026-08-22-multi-block-acetyl-research-before-after; nothing there is deleted.

MALCOLM, 2026-08-25, THREE CHANGES AND NOTHING ELSE:
  1. CAUCASIAN MIDDLE-AGED WOMEN ONLY, all three blocks.
  2. The skin has to hold up as real, in detail.
  3. The percentage improvement must be SEEN - but stay realistic, not too much difference.

WHAT r1 GOT RIGHT AND IS CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED: the diptych. All 33 r1 candidates put their seam within 0.5% of centre, so briefing two panels meeting at a crisp central edge works on every engine. The matrixyl brief's rule against split frames does NOT apply to this page and its `no split screen` / `no dividing line` negatives stay removed.

CHANGE 1 REPLACES r1's PER-STUDY POPULATION MATCH. r1 cast each block to its own trial's population (Wang 2013 Chinese, Blanes-Mira 2002 European, An 2019 Korean). Malcolm's call overrides that. The risk it introduces is that one woman appears to be enrolled in three different studies on one page, so the three are briefed as VISIBLY DIFFERENT INDIVIDUALS - different age within middle age, different eye colour, different hair colour, different skin character. They must not read as the same person three times.

CHANGE 2 - THE SKIN. r1 failed here in three specific ways and each has a fix:
  * WHITE SPECULAR FLECKS across the after half on both nbp_flash f3 candidates, reading as dry flaking - the exact opposite of the claim. Cause was MY wording: 'a faint healthy sheen it did not have before'. Words like sheen, glow, dewy and hydrated get rendered as speckled specular highlights. All of them are gone from this brief and `no specular speckle, no white flecks` is in the negatives.
  * SEEDREAM DREW THE WRINKLES AS PAINTED MARKS on both f2 candidates - three red-brown slashes on the temple, like scratches. Cause was 'three or four expression lines cross the temple as grooves', which reads as an instruction to DRAW strokes. Lines are now described by what the skin is DOING - creased, folded, drawn into - never as marks placed on it.
  * UNIFORM MACHINE TEXTURE. The acceptance test on this project is a dense allover field of near-parallel micro-lines at even density with no pore variation. This brief now specifies pore size varying BY ZONE, individual outsized pores, asymmetric freckling, a capillary flush, and matte-to-oily variation across the frame - positive detail, because negating the artefact has never worked as well as specifying the real thing.

CHANGE 3 - THE MAGNITUDE, AND THE DEVICE THAT MAKES IT HONEST. r1 ran f1 slightly strong and f3 so subtle it vanished at 350px. The rule now is structural rather than adjectival: THE NUMBER AND POSITION OF THE LINES IS IDENTICAL IN BOTH HALVES AND NO LINE MAY DISAPPEAR. What changes is DEPTH and SHADOW only. Every mole, freckle, pore and stray hair stays exactly where it is. This is what separates a believable result from an advertisement, and it also happens to be what the studies actually measured - roughness and depth, not line count.
Magnitude per block, stated as a fraction of depth so it is checkable rather than a matter of taste: f1 about half the depth, f2 about a third, f3 the smallest of the three but still plainly visible when the halves are compared side by side.

NO LETTERING FROM THE ENGINES - UNCHANGED FROM r1 AND STILL THE LOAD-BEARING RULE. Every percentage is composited afterwards by scripts/label-before-after.py from the `label` block below. On this project MATRIXYL failed in ~30 of 50 candidates and a correct PDRN was resampled into PORN; a garbled efficacy figure is a false clinical claim on a live storefront, not a cosmetic defect.

OTHER r1 SUPPLIER FAULTS ADDRESSED: nbp_pro inset one f3 diptych in a grey mat, so every prompt now states the photograph fills the square edge to edge. Luma rendered the two halves at different camera angles on f1 - it has no negative-prompt field so the identical-camera instruction is stated twice in the prompt body where it will actually be read.

COLOUR: Acetyl's scene colour is Pearl grey D8D6D4 per the concern-to-colour map. It is the GROUND behind the skin, never a cast on the skin.

CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048.
labels_are_composited: scripts/label-before-after.py - see `label` on each slot. The engines never draw text.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks
slots.prompt:
An unretouched clinical dermatology reference photograph, filling the entire square frame edge to edge, divided into TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH that meet at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre.

BOTH PANELS SHOW THE SAME WOMAN, THE SAME EYE, FROM AN IDENTICAL CAMERA POSITION WITH IDENTICAL LIGHTING. Same face, same iris colour, same brow shape, same lash line, same freckles and moles in exactly the same places. The camera has not moved between the two panels and the light has not changed. NOTHING DIFFERS BETWEEN THE PANELS EXCEPT THE DEPTH OF THE CREASES IN THE SKIN.

She is a white European woman of about fifty-two, with fair skin, blue-grey eyes and light brown hair drawn back off her face. She wears no makeup at all. The framing is a tight macro of the OUTER CORNER OF ONE EYE: the lower lid, the lash line, the outer corner, and the flat of the temple beside it, with the brow partly in frame at the top. No mouth, no nose, no hairline, no ear. The eye is open and relaxed, looking slightly away from the lens, the expression neutral, not smiling and not squinting.

THE SKIN IS THE SUBJECT AND IT MUST BE REAL. Pores vary in size and in density across the frame - noticeably larger and more open on the inner side toward the nose, finer and tighter out at the temple - with two or three individual pores clearly larger than their neighbours. Sun-freckling is scattered and asymmetric, denser on the cheekbone than above it, with one small raised brown mole below the outer corner. A faint diffuse capillary flush warms the skin over the cheekbone. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light along the temple, lying in different directions. The skin is slightly oily and light-catching low on the cheekbone and completely matte out at the temple. Individual lower lashes vary in length and direction with small gaps between them. This is a documentary photograph of a real face, not a beauty campaign.

In the LEFT panel, the outer corner of the eye is creased into a fan of four or five expression lines that spread across the temple, each one folded deeply enough to hold a distinct shadow along its length, with a finer crepey network gathered beneath the lower lid.

In the RIGHT panel, THE SAME FOUR OR FIVE CREASES ARE STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about half as deep as before - the fold is softer, the shadow it holds much lighter, the edges less sharply defined - and the crepey network under the lid is finer and less pronounced. The deepest crease of the fan is still plainly visible. Every freckle, mole, pore and stray hair is exactly where it was. The difference is obvious when the two halves are compared, and it is clearly an improvement rather than a transformation.

One soft directional key light from the upper left with a gentle fill, raking just enough across the temple to describe the relief of the skin. The background behind her, thrown softly out of focus, is a smooth pale pearl grey, colour hex D8D6D4. Shot on a 100mm macro lens, sharp, honest and completely unretouched.
slots.negative_extra: no different woman in the two panels, no mirrored image, no flipped duplicate, no identical untouched copy, no line disappearing between the panels, no flawless skin in the right panel, no change of camera angle, no change of expression, no both eyes in frame, no forehead lines, no closed eye

slots.title: f2 · Blanes-Mira 2002 — up to ~30% reduction in measured wrinkle DEPTH, 30 days
slots.prompt:
An unretouched clinical dermatology reference photograph, filling the entire square frame edge to edge, divided into TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH that meet at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre.

BOTH PANELS SHOW THE SAME WOMAN, THE SAME EYE, FROM AN IDENTICAL CAMERA POSITION WITH IDENTICAL LIGHTING. Same face, same iris colour, same brow shape, same lash line, same freckles and moles in exactly the same places. The camera has not moved between the two panels and the light has not changed. NOTHING DIFFERS BETWEEN THE PANELS EXCEPT THE DEPTH OF THE CREASES IN THE SKIN.

THIS FINDING IS ABOUT DEPTH, SO THE LIGHT IS HARD AND LOW. A single hard key skims across the skin from the left at a very shallow angle with one soft fill, so the relief of the surface is read by shadow rather than by colour, and every crease casts.

She is a white Mediterranean woman of about forty-seven, with olive-fair skin, green-hazel eyes and dark brown hair drawn back off her face. She wears no makeup at all. The framing is a tight macro of the OUTER CORNER OF ONE EYE and the flat of the temple beside it - lower lid, lash line, outer corner, temple. No mouth, no nose, no hairline, no ear. The eye is open and relaxed, looking away from the lens, the expression neutral, not smiling and not squinting.

THE SKIN IS THE SUBJECT AND IT MUST BE REAL. Pores vary in size and density across the frame, more open low on the cheekbone and finer at the outer temple, with a few individually larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven in a natural way - a soft irregular patch of sun pigmentation on the cheekbone, one small dark mole near the hairline side of the temple, and no symmetry anywhere. Fine vellus hairs lie in varying directions and catch the raking light. The skin is matte at the temple and slightly light-catching on the cheekbone. Lower lashes vary in length with small gaps. This is a documentary photograph of a real face, not a beauty campaign.

In the LEFT panel, the skin at the outer corner is folded into three or four strong creases running back across the temple. In the raking light each one is unmistakably a channel with real depth: a bright edge along its upper wall and a dark shadow held in its floor.

In the RIGHT panel, THE SAME THREE OR FOUR CREASES ARE STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about a third less deep - the floor of each channel is lighter, the shadow shorter, the contrast between its bright edge and its dark floor visibly reduced - so they read as softened folds rather than cut channels. They still cast in the same raking light. Every mark, mole, pore and hair is exactly where it was. The difference is clear when the halves are compared, and the surface is not flat and not perfect.

The background behind her, thrown softly out of focus, is a smooth pale pearl grey, colour hex D8D6D4. Shot on a 100mm macro lens, sharp, honest and completely unretouched.
